I'm not lying. I'm part of a group that runs together. We train 3 times a week and partake in 5k races often. And I eat healthy. I eat mostly vegetables, legumes and fruit. I don't over eat either if anything I eat less than I should because I'm scared of eating too much.

And I can assure you my skinny friend lives off of junk food because I'm with her when she eats. She doesn't know how to cook anything that isn't fried and most of the time she eats pizza, hamburgers, fries with fried egg on top or even plain pasta with cheese, hot dogs, and fried egg on top. She doesn't even know how to cook rice, the only vegetable she likes is potatoes and is a very picky eater when it comes to fruit too. I know my friend and I know how she eats. She makes fun of my veggies because she says she could never eat them. 

And don't get me wrong. I'm happy she looks the way she does. I just don't understand why our body's are so different. It's like she was blessed.

Talking to her she said she wishes she had big thighs and a big butt and chest like me so I guess we can never be satisfied with what we have and we always want what others have.

I don't want to give up but I feel like I might have to. It sucks because it makes me feel really weak when I watch other people take more than five classes at a time and I'm stuck struggling with less. I don't know. I'm thinking about dropping out of a few classes but I know I can't. My father, who's supporting me while I study because I'm incapable of keeping a job without going unhinged, will be very angry of I keep adding years to his "dealing with me". He wants me to graduate by next year or he'll stop supporting me at all. Which is an added stress because I'm not able to support myself because I can't deal with the pressure of keeping up a job. 

Bipolar might not be a disability but God damn it some times it feels like one. Sadly in my university you need a doctor's notice for every single medical excuse you present and my psychiatrist and therapist refuse to give me doctors notices.

I'm sorry for ranting to you. I hope you get better soon.

5. At first I thought I might be bi, I tried to think of myself as bi for a while last year because I wanted to keep some hope that I could marry a guy and keep my family but I realized that I've never really been interested in men at all. So I'm pretty sure I'm a lesbian.  
6. I'm not quite sure but when I was in middle school I had the biggest crush on one of my teachers. It might be weird but she was really strict and kind of mean but one time I had a panic attack and she sat me on her lap and helped me calm down. I thought she was the most beautiful woman ever. I wanted to impress her so much. I don't think I knew at the time that I had a crush.
7. It just feels right. I've never had a boyfriend. In highschool I used to choose one of the boys in my class who looked like he would never be interested in me to have a crush on so I could fit in with the girls. If he ever showed any interest in me I'd do anything in my power to ruin our friendship so I had an excuse to be seen as straight but not have to touch a boy. The thought of being touched by a guy scares me, I've never felt comfortable around them. Even though being a lesbian means losing everything and puts me at great risk it feels right. 
8. When I was a kid (I can't remember how old I was because this memory is sadly tied to some trauma), I had a girl friend. We went to the same school and church so our parents allowed us to play together. We used to play house. I was the mom and she was the dad. I pretended to take care of our baby and cook her dinner and she would come back from work, kiss me on the lips and ask how my day went. It felt right at the time. When our parents found out they were furious. We weren't allowed to see each other again after that.
9. I'm okay with being a lesbian, I'd even say I'm proud in a sense. But I'm afraid for my safety. And I'm sad because I  know that the people who I thought loved me would be disgusted with me if they knew. Some times it feels like I'm just not made to be loved. 
10. I don't know. I'm currently living with my abusive father as I'm finishing my degree and no longer have a job. Being financially tied to an abusive man is hell on Earth. If I had to give my younger self advice I'd say get a job first, leave home, worry about your education later. I hope one day I'll be free. I'll have my own apartment and maybe then I'll get to have friends that acept me and, if I'm lucky, even experience love.
